subject: history

moments.title: Thatcher elected
moments.who: Margaret Thatcher and the Conservative Party
moments.body: May 1979: Thatcher wins after the 'Winter of Discontent' (1978-79 public sector strikes). Her programme: monetarism, privatisation, trade union reform, council house sales (Right to Buy 1980), tax cuts. The 'Thatcher revolution' begins.
moments.takeaway: Thatcher was Britain's first female Prime Minister and the longest-serving of the 20th century (11 years).

moments.title: Miners' strike
moments.who: Arthur Scargill, NUM, and the government
moments.body: March 1984: the National Coal Board announces 20 pit closures. Scargill calls a strike without a national ballot. The strike lasts a year. Police-miner clashes at Orgreave (June 1984) become iconic. The NUM returns to work in March 1985 without an agreement.
moments.takeaway: The defeat broke organised labour as a political force. Trade union membership has fallen from around 13 million in 1979 to around 6.5 million today.

moments.title: Poll tax and resignation
moments.body: April 1989: the Community Charge ('poll tax') introduced in Scotland; England and Wales 1990. Mass non-payment, riots in central London March 1990. November 1990: Conservative leadership challenge by Michael Heseltine; Thatcher resigns after failing to win the first ballot outright.
moments.takeaway: The poll tax was the trigger; long-running cabinet revolt over Europe (Geoffrey Howe's resignation speech, 13 November) was the deeper cause.

now.title: After Thatcherism
now.body: The 'Thatcher settlement' — privatisation, financial liberalisation, weak unions, restricted council housing — outlasted her. New Labour (1997-2010) accepted most of it. Critics (Stuart Hall, 'The Great Moving Right Show') argued Thatcherism reshaped political common sense. Defenders (John Campbell's biography) emphasise the inflation and industrial chaos she inherited.
now.open_questions: Did Thatcher save or break Britain? Polls divide sharply by region (favourable in the South-East, hostile in former industrial communities) and by age. The 2013 funeral protests showed the divisions were still raw.

reflection: Few British political careers have produced as durable an inheritance. The neoliberal turn of the 1980s set parameters that no subsequent government has fundamentally challenged — for praise or blame.
